**Step 1: Create the cleanup script**

{"name": "bash", "arguments": {"command": "cat > /workspace/docker_cleanup.sh << 'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# docker_cleanup.sh
# Cleans up Docker resources based on environment-driven configuration.
# All behaviour is controlled by variables exported from docker_config.env.
# =============================================================================

set -euo pipefail

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 0. Resolve configuration from environment (with safe defaults)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
CLEANUP_OLDER_THAN_DAYS="${CLEANUP_OLDER_THAN_DAYS:-30}"
CLEANUP_UNUSED_VOLUMES="${CLEANUP_UNUSED_VOLUMES:-false}"
CLEANUP_DANGLING_IMAGES="${CLEANUP_DANGLING_IMAGES:-false}"
CLEANUP_STOPPED_CONTAINERS="${CLEANUP_STOPPED_CONTAINERS:-false}"
MAX_LOG_SIZE="${MAX_LOG_SIZE:-100m}"
LOG_RETENTION_DAYS="${LOG_RETENTION_DAYS:-7}"
REGISTRY_URL="${REGISTRY_URL:-}"
BACKUP_BEFORE_CLEANUP="${BACKUP_BEFORE_CLEANUP:-false}"
DRY_RUN="${DRY_RUN:-false}"
NOTIFICATION_EMAIL="${NOTIFICATION_EMAIL:-}"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
TIMESTAMP=$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')
LOG_FILE="/workspace/docker_cleanup_$(date '+%Y%m%d_%H%M%S').log"

log() {
    local level="$1"; shift
    local msg="$*"
    local line="[${TIMESTAMP}] [${level}] ${msg}"
    echo "${line}" | tee -a "${LOG_FILE}"
}

info()    { log "INFO " "$*"; }
warn()    { log "WARN " "$*"; }
error()   { log "ERROR" "$*"; }
success() { log "OK   " "$*"; }

# Wraps every destructive Docker comma
